The algorithm iteratively updates a page's topic probability, considering both its own text and the contributions from linked pages, weighted by an 'alpha' parameter.", "key_parameters": ["PLSA (Probabilistic Latent Semantic Analysis)", "PageRank", "alpha (weighting text vs. link contribution)", "iterative algorithm"]}, "initial_evaluation_challenges": ["Difficulty in quantitatively evaluating unsupervised topic models, which are often judged qualitatively by 'looking at the clustering'.", "Inability to tell which of two topic vectors (one from PLSA, one from the combined model) is 'better' without ground truth for topics.", "Perplexity or likelihood metrics can be misleading or 'bad' (as per Pedro's example with cars).", "Topic models can find good clusters (e.g., English vs. French pages) that are completely unrelated to a desired directory's categories (e.g., Good vs. Bad pages).", "Human evaluation of clustering is subjective and varies between individuals.", "Bag-of-words representation loses important visual and layout information from web pages (e.g., Google.com being a search engine).", "The averaging effect of the algorithm can 'flatten' topic distributions, making the model more uncertain about page topics, which might not always be desirable."], "discussed_evaluation_ideas": [{"idea_name": "Using likelihood or perplexity as an evaluation metric", "reason_for_concern_or_rejection": "Pedro's example showed that this could be a 'bad' metric, implying it might not reflect true model quality or relevance."}, {"idea_name": "Human evaluation by categorizing pages based on word distributions for topics", "reason_for_concern_or_rejection": "Human clustering is subjective and inconsistent;
